title: The Battle of Verdun
subject: histoire
description: For **299 days**, French and Germans tore each other apart around Verdun. **700,000** losses for almost zero territorial gain: the symbol of the horror of the trenches.

hero.hook: 299 days for a few kilometers of mud and 700,000 men out of action.

blocks.text: In **1916**, during **299 days**, French and Germans clashed over a few square kilometers around **Verdun**, a stronghold in eastern France. This is not a brilliant breakthrough. It's a battle of attrition, with approximately **700,000** dead or injured.
Verdun becomes the symbol of the horror of the trenches. Decades later, it also became that of Franco-German reconciliation.

Since 1914, the Western Front has been frozen in the : lines of ditches from the North Sea to Switzerland. The German general **Erich von Falkenhayn** wants to “bleed France dry”. He chooses Verdun, a place that Paris cannot abandon without losing face. The operation is called , “the court”. [[Trench warfare]] [[Gericht]]

blocks.caption: The Verdun trenches: a landscape devoured by artillery.

blocks.text: The opening bombardment of **February 21, 1916** was so violent that it could be heard as far away as the Vosges, more than **150 km**.

**February 21**, **1 200 cannons** shell the French lines. The **25**, the **fort of Douaumont**, key to the defense, fell almost without a fight. Paris must now bet everything on Verdun: Falkenhayn's trap works.

sections.title: Pétain, the Sacred Way and the rotation of troops

blocks.text: General **Philippe Pétain** organizes the survival of the sector. The **Sacred Way** connects , a town in the rear, to Verdun: nearly **6,000 trucks** per day, one vehicle every **14 seconds**. When it breaks down, we push the truck into the ditch so as not to block the road. [[Bar-le-Duc]]

blocks.caption: The Voie Sacrée, a vital artery of French supply.

blocks.text: With the , Pétain rotated the divisions quickly: we stayed a short time at the front, then we were relieved. Result: approximately **70 %** of the French army fights in Verdun at one time or another. The battle becomes a national experience. [[Noria]]

sections.title: The hell of cannons, almost without gain

blocks.text: In the summer, the , a Franco-British offensive further north, relieves Verdun. Under General **Robert Nivelle**, the French recaptured Douaumont then Fort Vaux. The battle ended on December 18, 1916. The lines have barely moved. [[The Battle of the Somme (1916)]]
Fleury-devant-Douaumont was taken and retaken **16 times** in two months, then wiped off the map. It is one of the “dead villages for France”, still administered without inhabitants.

Approximately **370,000** French and **330,000** Germans fall or are mutilated. The  kills more than melee. s remain unsuitable for any civilian life: too many unexploded munitions, too much poisoned soil. [[Heavy artillery of the Great War]] [[Red Zones]]

sections.title: From the ossuary to the handshake

blocks.text: The **Ossuary of Douaumont** (1932) houses the remains of **130,000** mixed French and German soldiers. **September 22, 1984**, French President **François Mitterrand** and German Chancellor **Helmut Kohl** hold hands in front of the monument. Verdun becomes a symbol of European peace.

events.title: Sum
events.detail: The Allies relieve the Verdun front.

blocks.text: **Verdun** (**1916**): **299** days of industrial war, approximately **700,000** losses for zero territorial gain, and later the symbol of Franco-German reconciliation.
